name: MySQL

inputs.name: ca
inputs.label: CA certificate file (PEM) - needed with TLS verify, a public CA too: its root (e.g. ISRG Root X1)

schema_check.statement: SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.schemata WHERE schema_name = BINARY {v}) THEN 'ok' ELSE COALESCE((SELECT CONCAT('case:', MIN(schema_name)) FROM information_schema.schemata WHERE LOWER(schema_name) = LOWER({v})), 'missing') END
schema_check.case: MySQL database names are case-sensitive on Linux

tips: Table and column names keep MySQL's spelling (actor, first_name): quote them, e.g. SELECT "first_name" FROM <schema>."actor".
YEAR columns arrive as DATE (2006 reads as 2006-01-01); TEXT arrives as VARCHAR(65535).
notes: MySQL has no schemas below a database: the dialect takes CATALOG_NAME only.
Connector/J is downloaded from Maven Central on this machine and never redistributed (GPL with the FOSS exception).

verify needs --set ca=<PEM file or bundle>, a public CA's root too (the loader's own CA store is empty on Exasol Personal 2.4): Connector/J reads trust only from a file or URL, so the kit writes the bundle as a JKS truststore for this source and gives its path relative to where both the adapter and the loader start.
